title: Reduce registry publication filesystem overhead
goal: Avoid repeated existing-parent preparation only for unsynced atomic metadata writes while retaining complete publication, permissions, errors and atomicity; measure end-to-end benefit.
checkpoint: Independent review passed. The paired median first-useful-output improvement is 88.685 ms for fresh homes and 104.270 ms for reused homes. Serialized integration, the full workspace gate, publication, and production qualification remain pending. No production-budget or under-60-second delivery claim is made.

verification.guards: Architecture: 41 passed; documentation: 5 passed; lean ceilings: 2 passed; orphan sources: 3 passed; task records: 3 passed.
verification.regressions: susi-core registry IPC: 5 passed; cross-copy: 2 passed; handler errors: 1 passed; prefix routing: 1 passed.
verification.config_library: 317 passed, 0 failed, and 2 existing ignored tests: a Windows symlink-privilege fixture and a subprocess helper.

runtime.nonce: Every full per-run unique nonce returned in stdout and mission SUCCESS trace
runtime.inventory: Each run had 439 metadata files plus an empty owner.lock, with exact normalized bytes and registered inventory matching the baseline.

verification.profile: Native-admitted host-mode dev opt0, lto=false, incremental=true, and dev/test codegen units 16.
verification.limitations: Windows-only scoped verification; the Unix 0600 regression was not executed. Two seeding runs were excluded, including candidate first-launch spawn overhead. OS caches were not cold; other desktop load was uncontrolled. Runtime evidence binds the recorded source hash before the final task-metadata update, not a later commit. Build scripts do not embed task records. The full workspace gate, integration, and production qualification remain pending; no production budget pass is claimed.
verification.native_admission: Current tracked trusted_sysroot prepare/apply/recheck was held across every Cargo phase. Baseline and candidate compiler evidence and all 20 sysroot archive hashes match.
verification.focused: 9 atomic-write tests passed, 0 failed, including five new Windows-applicable regressions.
